subject: Maths
title: 10 times table
subtitle: Multiplication and Division (2, 5, 10 Times Tables) · KS3 Maths
learning_objective: I can recall and use the 10 times table to multiply and divide.

key_vocab.definition: The 10 times table is a list of multiples of 10: numbers we get when we count in 10s. Numbers in the 10 times table always end in 0.

sections.title: Learning Objective
sections.content: I can recall and use the 10 times table to multiply and divide.

sections.title: Key Words
sections.content: 10 times table -- The 10 times table is a list of multiples of 10: numbers we get when we count in 10s. Numbers in the 10 times table always end in 0.

sections.title: Method
sections.content:
Multiplication is repeated addition. 10 × 4 means ‘4 groups of 10’. You can also think of it as ‘10 groups of 4’ — the answer is the same.
10 + 10 + 10 + 10 = 10×4 = 40
Four groups of 10

Key examples:
  ✓ 1 × 10 = 10  (starting point)
  ✓ 2 × 10 = 20  (double)
  ✓ 5 × 10 = 50  (halfway to 10)
  ✗ 3 × 10 = 31  (wrong)
  ✗ 10 × 0 = 10  (any × 0 = 0)

sections.title: Worked Example
sections.content:
Example 1 – single multiplication
  Calculate 7 × 10
  7 groups of 10
  10 + 10 + 10 + 10  ...
  = 70
  = 70
  (Skip-count in 10s 7 times to reach 70.)

Example 2 – missing factor
  Solve: ___ × 10 = 40
  How many 10s in 40?
  Count up: 10, 20, 30, ...
  = 4
  = 4
  (Divide: 40 ÷ 10 = 4.)
